questions.questionText: Listen to the word hay. Which word has the same vowel sound?
questions.explanation: Hay and tray both have the long a sound /eI/ spelled ay. oak tank and barn have short vowel sounds.

questions.questionText: Which word has the same vowel sound as south?
questions.explanation: South and sprout both have the ou sound /aU/ and they rhyme.

questions.questionText: Which word has the ear sound as in fear?
questions.explanation: Fear and tear both have the ear sound /IE@/. ring jet and wall do not.

questions.questionText: One of these words has the ea sound /i:/ as in peak. Which one?
questions.explanation: Peak and steal have the long e sound /i:/. Spread thread and pleasant use the short e sound /e/.

questions.questionText: The magic e makes the vowel long. Which word has a long i sound like bite?
questions.explanation: Side uses magic e so the i says its own name /aI/. Kit kin and kid have a short i.

questions.questionText: Which word has the ie sound /i:/ as in field?
questions.explanation: Field and piece have the long e sound /i:/. Pie lie and die have the ie sound /aI/.

questions.questionText: Which word rhymes with gray?
questions.explanation: Gray and stray both end with the ay sound /eI/. jar hand and nap do not rhyme.

questions.questionText: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others?
questions.explanation: Cow now and brown have the ou sound /aU/. Low has the long o sound /@U/.

questions.questionText: Which word has the ear sound /IE@/ and not the air sound /e@/?
questions.explanation: Fear has the ear sound /IE@/. Stairs flare and glare have the air sound /e@/.

questions.questionText: Which word uses magic e to make a long o sound like hole?
questions.explanation: Rode uses magic e so the o says its name /@U/. oak crab and stick have short vowel sounds.

questions.questionText: Which word has the ea sound as in teach?
questions.explanation: Teach and peach have the long e sound /i:/. Thread spread and sweat have the short e /e/.

questions.questionText: Which word does NOT have the /eI/ sound?
questions.explanation: Stay clay and away have the ay sound /eI/. Bread has the short e sound /e/.

questions.questionText: Which word has a short vowel sound and not a long magic e sound?
questions.explanation: Mop has a short o. Side stripe and globe use magic e and have a long vowel sound.

questions.questionText: Which word rhymes with cow?
questions.explanation: Cow and now both have the ou sound /aU/. Slow snow and grow have the long o /@U/.

questions.questionText: Which word has the ou sound as in shout?
questions.explanation: Shout and scout both have the ou sound /aU/. Oven umbrella and off do not.

questions.questionText: If the teacher says repeat what does she want you to do?
questions.explanation: Repeat means to say the same words again after the teacher.

questions.questionText: Which word describes a very loud deep noise?
questions.explanation: A roar is a loud deep sound. Whisper murmur and sigh are soft quiet sounds.

questions.questionText: What do you use your ears for?
questions.explanation: You use your ears to hear. You use your eyes nose and mouth for the other actions.

questions.questionText: You hear the wind whispers through the trees. What does whispers mean?
questions.explanation: To whisper is to speak very softly so that only someone near can hear.

questions.questionText: Which word do you say when you ask politely for something?
questions.explanation: Please is the polite word we use when we ask for something or make a request.

questions.questionText: Your teacher says please open your book. What do you do?
questions.explanation: When the teacher asks you to open your book you open it and get ready to read.

questions.questionText: The teacher says sit down please. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Sit down means you lower yourself onto your chair.

questions.questionText: Work in pairs. What does the teacher want you to do?
questions.explanation: A pair is two people, so working in pairs means you work with one friend.

questions.questionText: You cannot hear the teacher. What do you say?
questions.explanation: When you cannot hear you politely ask the speaker to say the words again.

questions.questionText: The teacher asks can you hear me. What do you answer?
questions.explanation: The teacher asks whether you can hear, so you answer that yes you can hear.

questions.questionText: Line up please. Where do the children go?

options.label: C
options.text: go to the door in a line

questions.explanation: To line up means to stand one behind another in a straight line, usually at the door.

questions.questionText: The teacher says turn to page ten and circle the answer. What two things do you do?

options.label: B
options.text: find page ten and draw a circle

questions.explanation: You open the book to page ten and then draw a circle around the right answer.

questions.questionText: What do you do when the teacher says raise your hand?
questions.explanation: Raise your hand means lift your hand up in the air, for example to answer a question.

questions.questionText: A classmate asks can I borrow your pencil. What is a polite answer?
questions.explanation: When someone borrows something politely you can say yes and hand it over.

questions.questionText: When the teacher says be quiet what should you do?
questions.explanation: Be quiet means you stop talking and make little or no noise.

questions.questionText: The teacher says put your things away. What does that mean?

options.label: C
options.text: put them in your bag or desk

questions.explanation: To put things away means to return them to the correct place such as your bag or desk.

questions.questionText: Listen carefully. What does the teacher want?
questions.explanation: Listen carefully means you use your ears and pay full attention to what is said.

questions.questionText: The teacher asks who can help me carry these boxes. What do you say if you want to help?
questions.explanation: To offer help you say me please or I can help.

questions.questionText: Stand up please. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Stand up means you rise from your chair to your feet.

questions.questionText: Your friend says sorry I am late. What do you say?

options.label: B
options.text: please come in and sit down

questions.explanation: When a friend arrives late you let them in kindly and ask them to sit down.

questions.questionText: Which word means the same as look at?
questions.explanation: To look at something means to see it with your eyes.

questions.questionText: The teacher says match the pictures to the words. What do you draw?
questions.explanation: Matching means you join each picture to the right word with a line.

questions.questionText: Do it on your own. What does the teacher mean?
questions.explanation: On your own means you complete the work by yourself without help.

questions.questionText: What do you say when you want to ask the teacher a question?
questions.explanation: You say excuse me please to get the teacher attention politely.

questions.questionText: The teacher says colour the apple red. What do you use?
questions.explanation: Colour the apple red means you use a red crayon or pencil to fill it in.

questions.questionText: The teacher asks you to hand out the worksheets. What do you do?
questions.explanation: To hand out means to give one copy to each person in the class.

questions.questionText: Come in please. Who says this?

options.label: A
options.text: a teacher to a child at the door

questions.explanation: Come in please is what a teacher says to let a child enter the room.

questions.questionText: The teacher says do not run in the classroom. What must you do?
questions.explanation: Do not run means you must walk instead of running inside the classroom.

questions.questionText: Work quietly and finish your work. Which action is right?
questions.explanation: Working quietly means you speak softly and keep on finishing your own work.

questions.questionText: Which word means to say the same words after the teacher?
questions.explanation: Repeat means to say the words again, usually after someone else.

questions.questionText: You hear: The dog runs in the park. It chases a red ball. It barks and wags its tail. What is this talk about?

options.label: A
options.text: a dog playing in the park

options.label: B
options.text: a cat sleeping on the mat

questions.explanation: All three sentences are about a dog running chasing a ball and wagging its tail in the park.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: It rains all day. The children cannot go out. They read books and draw pictures inside the house. What is the main idea?

options.label: A
options.text: a sunny day at the beach

questions.explanation: The rain keeps the children inside where they read and draw, so the main idea is a rainy indoor day.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: Bo wants a new kite. He saves his money for two weeks. At last he buys a big blue kite. What is the best title?
questions.explanation: The whole talk is about Bo saving money and finally buying a blue kite.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: The little kitten is frail. It is very small and weak. The girl gives it warm milk. What does frail mean?
questions.explanation: The next sentence says the kitten is small and weak, which tells you frail means weak and thin.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: Grandma grows tomatoes in her garden. They are round and red. She picks them and makes soup. What is the talk about?
questions.explanation: Every sentence mentions tomatoes growing being picked and made into soup.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: The old clock ticks loudly. It wakes the boy up every morning. He likes its clear sound. What does ticks mean?
questions.explanation: A clock ticks when it makes a regular clicking sound as it measures time.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: We go to the beach on Sunday. The sand is warm. The sea is blue. We build a big sandcastle. What is the main idea?

options.label: B
options.text: a happy day at the beach

options.label: C
options.text: a long day at the shop

options.label: D
options.text: a hot day at the farm

questions.explanation: The sand the sea and the sandcastle all show that the talk is about a day at the beach.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: The path is narrow. Only one child can walk at a time between the tall trees. What does narrow mean?
questions.explanation: Because only one child can pass at a time, the path is not wide.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: Ting has a guitar. She plucks the strings gently. The music is sweet. What are they talking about?
questions.explanation: The guitar the strings and the sweet music all point to Ting playing music.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: The bus is late. Many people wait at the stop. They look at their watches. What is the main idea?
questions.explanation: The late bus the waiting people and the watches all describe waiting for a late bus.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: Devi folds the paper carefully. Then she cuts it into a shape. It becomes a lovely bird. What does folds mean?

options.label: A
options.text: bends the paper over on itself

questions.explanation: To fold paper means to bend it over on itself, as you do when making a paper shape.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: The zoo is crowded on holidays. Many families come to see the animals. The lions sleep and the monkeys jump. What is this talk about?

options.label: B
options.text: a busy zoo on a holiday

questions.explanation: The crowded zoo the families and the animals all show a busy zoo on a holiday.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: Nabil waters his plant every morning. It grows a little each week. Soon it has many green leaves. What is the best title?
questions.explanation: The watering the growth and the green leaves are all about Nabil growing a plant.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: The old chair wobbles. When you sit on it it moves from side to side. Be careful. What does wobbles mean?
questions.explanation: A chair that moves from side to side is shaking in an unsteady way, which is called wobbling.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: You hear: There is a storm at sea. The waves are high. The small boat rocks up and down. What is the main idea?
questions.explanation: The storm the high waves and the rocking boat all describe a storm on the sea.
questions.subtopic: Main idea of short audio texts

questions.questionText: Passage: One afternoon Mei hears a small sound near the bush. She looks down and sees a tiny kitten. It is grey and very thin. Mei gives it some milk. The kitten licks the bowl clean. Mei wants to keep the kitten. Her mother smiles and nods. Mei calls the kitten Misty. Every evening Mei feeds Misty and plays with her in the yard. Where does Mei find the kitten?
questions.explanation: The passage says Mei hears a small sound near the bush and looks down to see the kitten.

questions.questionText: Passage (the kitten story): What colour is the kitten?
questions.explanation: The passage says the kitten is grey and very thin.

questions.questionText: Passage (the kitten story): What does Mei give the kitten?
questions.explanation: The passage says Mei gives the kitten some milk.

questions.questionText: Passage (the kitten story): Her mother smiles and nods. What does nodded mean?

options.label: A
options.text: shook her head to say no

options.label: D
options.text: moved her head up and down to say yes

questions.explanation: Nodding the head up and down is the way we say yes.

questions.questionText: Passage (the kitten story): When does Mei play with Misty?
questions.explanation: The passage says every evening Mei feeds Misty and plays with her in the yard.

questions.questionText: Passage: Bo helps his grandfather build a birdhouse. They cut wood and nail the pieces. They paint it bright blue. Then they fix it on a high branch. Soon two small birds come. They sing happily in the new house. Bo watches them every day. What do Bo and his grandfather build?
questions.explanation: The passage begins by saying Bo and his grandfather build a birdhouse.

questions.questionText: Passage (the birdhouse story): What colour is the birdhouse?
questions.explanation: The passage says they paint the birdhouse bright blue.

questions.questionText: Passage (the birdhouse story): Where do they fix the birdhouse?
questions.explanation: The passage says they fix it on a high branch.

questions.questionText: Passage (the birdhouse story): Bo watches them every day. In the story what does proud mean?

options.label: B
options.text: feeling good about something you did

questions.explanation: Proud means you feel happy and good about something you have done.

questions.questionText: Passage (the birdhouse story): Why do the small birds come to the house?

options.label: D
options.text: They like the new house and sing there

questions.explanation: The birds come and sing happily in the new house, so they like it.

questions.questionText: Passage: Ayu plants a small seed in a pot. She waters it every day. The soil is warm. After many days a green shoot comes up. It grows taller and taller. Soon it has a big yellow flower. The flower turns to face the sun. Ayu is happy. What does Ayu plant in the pot?
questions.explanation: The passage says Ayu plants a small seed in a pot.

questions.questionText: Passage (the sunflower story): What colour is the flower?
questions.explanation: The passage says the plant grows a big yellow flower.

questions.questionText: Passage (the sunflower story): What does the flower turn to face?
questions.explanation: The passage says the flower turns to face the sun.

questions.questionText: Passage (the sunflower story): a green shoot comes up. What is a shoot?

options.label: D
options.text: the young new plant that comes up

questions.explanation: A shoot is the young new green part of a plant that first comes up from the soil.

questions.questionText: Passage (the sunflower story): How does Ayu feel about her sunflower?
questions.explanation: The passage says Ayu is happy and she shows the tall sunflower to her friends, so she feels proud.

questions.questionText: Passage: Every Saturday Kavita goes to the market with her father. They buy fresh fish and ripe bananas. Kavita likes the colourful stalls. Her father talks to the friendly sellers. They carry the food home in a big basket. Kavita helps her father. When does Kavita go to the market?
questions.explanation: The passage says Kavita goes to the market every Saturday.

questions.questionText: Passage (the market story): What do they buy at the market?
questions.explanation: The passage says they buy fresh fish and ripe bananas.

questions.questionText: Passage (the market story): Who does Kavita go to the market with?
questions.explanation: The passage says Kavita goes to the market with her father.

questions.questionText: Passage (the market story): ripe bananas. What does ripe mean?
questions.explanation: Ripe fruit is fully grown and ready and good to eat.

questions.questionText: Passage (the market story): the colourful stalls. What are stalls?

options.label: B
options.text: places where sellers show and sell things

questions.explanation: At a market the stalls are the tables or small stands where sellers show and sell their things.

questions.questionText: Which sentence gives an opinion?

options.label: B
options.text: I think the beach is lovely.

questions.explanation: An opinion tells what someone thinks or feels. I think the beach is lovely is an opinion.

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence that gives a reason for a liking.

options.label: A
options.text: I like Saturday because I can play in the park.

questions.explanation: The word because gives the reason why the speaker likes Saturday.

questions.questionText: Your friend asks what do you think of the new film. What do you say?

options.label: A
options.text: The film is on the shelf.

options.label: C
options.text: I think it is exciting and I enjoy it.

questions.explanation: When asked for your opinion you say what you think and feel about the film.

questions.questionText: Which word is an opinion word not a plain fact?
questions.explanation: Wonderful tells how someone feels. Round small and wooden are plain facts you can check.

questions.questionText: Do you like rainy days. Which answer gives a reason?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes I like them because the plants grow.

questions.explanation: The answer says yes and then uses because to give the reason why.

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence that tells what someone thinks.

options.label: B
options.text: We think the song is nice.

questions.explanation: We think the song is nice tells what the speakers think about the song.

questions.questionText: Your friend says I think reading is boring. What is a polite answer?

options.label: C
options.text: I do not agree. I think it is fun because we learn new things.

questions.explanation: A polite answer disagrees gently and gives a reason for your own opinion.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is a FACT not an opinion?
questions.explanation: Being big is a fact you can check. Lovely like and best show what someone feels.

questions.questionText: What do you say if someone asks your opinion about durian?

options.label: B
options.text: I think durian smells strong but I like its sweet taste.

questions.explanation: You share what you think and feel about durian, good or bad, to answer the question.

questions.questionText: Complete: I think this cartoon is ... Choose the best opinion word.
questions.explanation: Funny tells what you think and feel about the cartoon. The other choices are facts about it.

questions.questionText: Which sentence gives a good reason for the opinion?

options.label: D
options.text: I like my teacher because she helps me learn.

questions.explanation: Because she helps me learn gives a clear reason why the speaker likes the teacher.

questions.questionText: You want to ask a friend opinion about the soup. What do you say?

options.label: C
options.text: What do you think of this soup?

questions.explanation: To ask for an opinion you say what do you think of this soup.

questions.questionText: What do you say if you like sunny weather?

options.label: B
options.text: I like sunny days because I can play outside.

questions.explanation: You say what you like and use because to give the reason.

questions.questionText: Which sentence pairs an opinion with a reason correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: I like my schoolbag because it has many pockets.

questions.explanation: Because it has many pockets gives a reason that supports the opinion that you like the bag.

questions.questionText: Your cousin asks do you like rabbits. What do you answer with a reason?

options.label: D
options.text: Yes because they are soft and quiet.

questions.explanation: The answer says yes and gives the reason with because, even though because is joined in the reply.

questions.questionText: Your friend says noodles are the best food. You like rice more. What do you say politely?

options.label: C
options.text: I like rice better but noodles are nice too.

questions.explanation: You say your own opinion kindly without making the friend feel small.

questions.questionText: Which sentence agrees with an opinion politely?
questions.explanation: I think so too is a polite way to show you agree with the other person.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses I like ... because ... correctly?

options.label: B
options.text: I like morning walks because the air is fresh.

questions.explanation: It says what the speaker likes (morning walks) and the reason (the air is fresh).

questions.questionText: Your aunt asks do you like school trips. What do you say to give your opinion?

options.label: D
options.text: Yes I like them because we see many animals.

questions.explanation: You say yes and give the reason, which is a clear opinion with support.

questions.questionText: Someone points at a painting and asks is it good. What do you say to give your opinion?

options.label: C
options.text: I think it is beautiful because the colours are bright.

questions.explanation: You say what you think (beautiful) and give a reason (the colours are bright).

questions.questionText: My father ___ to work by bus every day.
questions.explanation: The subject 'My father' is one person, so the verb takes 's'. 'My father goes to work by bus every day.'

questions.questionText: The children ___ breakfast at seven in the morning.
questions.explanation: The subject 'The children' is more than one, so we use 'eat'. The children eat breakfast at seven.

questions.questionText: My grandma ___ the housework on Sunday mornings.
questions.explanation: 'My grandma' is one person, so we use 'does'. My grandma does the housework on Sunday mornings.

questions.questionText: I ___ my teeth before I go to bed.
questions.explanation: With 'I' we use the verb without 's'. I brush my teeth before I go to bed.

questions.questionText: We ___ to school together every morning.
questions.explanation: With 'We' we use the verb without 's'. We walk to school together every morning.

questions.questionText: The baby ___ milk before she sleeps at night.
questions.explanation: 'The baby' is one person, so the verb takes 's'. It is a daily habit, so we use 'drinks'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence about dinner.

options.label: A
options.text: My mother cook dinner every evening.

options.label: B
options.text: My mother cooking dinner every evening.

options.label: C
options.text: My mother cooks dinner every evening.

options.label: D
options.text: My mother is cooks dinner every evening.

questions.explanation: 'My mother' is one person, so the verb must be 'cooks'. The correct sentence is 'My mother cooks dinner every evening.'

questions.questionText: My brother ___ his homework after tea.
questions.explanation: 'My brother' is one person, so we use 'does'. My brother does his homework after tea.

questions.questionText: They ___ football in the park on Saturdays.
questions.explanation: 'They' is more than one, so we use 'play'. They play football in the park on Saturdays.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence about the sun.

options.label: A
options.text: The sun rise in the east.

options.label: B
options.text: The sun rises in the east.

options.label: C
options.text: The sun rising in the east.

options.label: D
options.text: The sun are rise in the east.

questions.explanation: 'The sun' is one thing, so the verb takes 's'. The correct sentence is 'The sun rises in the east.'

questions.questionText: I ___ up at six o'clock every day.
questions.explanation: With 'I' we use 'wake'. I wake up at six o'clock every day.

questions.questionText: We have ___ at half past twelve.
questions.explanation: The daily meal at midday is lunch. We have lunch at half past twelve.

questions.questionText: My sister ___ her face in the morning.
questions.explanation: 'My sister' is one person, so the verb takes 'es'. My sister washes her face in the morning.

questions.questionText: The pupils ___ to the national song every Monday.
questions.explanation: 'The pupils' is more than one, so we use 'listen'. The pupils listen to the national song every Monday.

questions.questionText: Grandpa ___ the newspaper after breakfast.
questions.explanation: 'Grandpa' is one person, so the verb takes 's'. Grandpa reads the newspaper after breakfast.

questions.questionText: Our cat ___ on the mat when we watch television.
questions.explanation: 'Our cat' is one animal, so the verb takes 's'. Our cat sleeps on the mat.

questions.questionText: I ___ my school bag before I go to bed.
questions.explanation: With 'I' we use 'pack'. I pack my school bag before I go to bed.

questions.questionText: Mum ___ dinner for the family every evening.
questions.explanation: 'Mum' is one person, so the verb takes 's'. Mum cooks dinner for the family every evening.

questions.questionText: We ___ water after we play games.
questions.explanation: 'We' is more than one, so we use 'drink'. We drink water after we play games.

questions.questionText: The birds ___ loudly when the sun comes up.
questions.explanation: 'The birds' is more than one, so we use 'sing'. The birds sing loudly when the sun comes up.

questions.questionText: You want to go to the bookshop near here. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Giving the way uses direction words. The answer with 'left' and 'straight' tells someone where to go.

questions.questionText: The shop is on your right. What do you do?
questions.explanation: If a place is on your right, you turn right to face it.

questions.questionText: At the corner, ___ and you will see the clinic on your left.
questions.explanation: To bring the clinic on your left, you turn left at the corner.

questions.questionText: Go ___ until you reach the traffic lights.
questions.explanation: 'Go straight' means keep going in the same line until the lights.

questions.questionText: The bank is not far. Walk straight and then turn ___ at the first junction.
questions.explanation: After walking straight, you turn right at the first junction.

questions.questionText: You are lost near the post office. What do you ask?
questions.explanation: Choose the words or reply that fits the meaning and the grammar.

questions.questionText: A friend asks the way to the library. You point ahead and say...
questions.explanation: Choose the words or reply that fits the meaning and the grammar.

questions.questionText: The school gate is between the shop and the house. To reach it you walk ___.
questions.explanation: Choose the words or reply that fits the meaning and the grammar.

questions.questionText: When you see the big tree, turn ___.
questions.explanation: The big tree is the cue for the turn, and the direction word is 'left'.

questions.questionText: What do you say to show the way to someone?
questions.explanation: Choose the words or reply that fits the meaning and the grammar.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct direction sentence for turning at the corner.
questions.explanation: A direction sentence is 'Turn left at the corner.'

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence for walking along the road.
questions.explanation: The order is 'Go along the straight road.'

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence about where the clinic is.

options.label: A
options.text: The clinic is next to the bank.

options.label: B
options.text: The clinic next to the is bank.

options.label: C
options.text: Is the clinic next bank to.

options.label: D
options.text: Next to the bank is clinic the.

questions.explanation: The order is 'The clinic is next to the bank.'

questions.questionText: Choose the correct order for the two directions.

options.label: A
options.text: Right turn and straight go then.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn right and then go straight.

options.label: C
options.text: Straight go and right turn then.

options.label: D
options.text: Then straight go right and turn.

questions.explanation: The order is 'Turn right and then go straight.'

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence telling where the bookshop is.

options.label: A
options.text: The bookshop on your is left.

options.label: B
options.text: Is the bookshop left on your.

options.label: C
options.text: The bookshop is on your left.

options.label: D
options.text: On your left the bookshop is.

questions.explanation: The order is 'The bookshop is on your left.'

questions.questionText: The sky is dark and cloudy. Will it rain?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because the sun is bright.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, because the clouds are dark.

questions.explanation: Dark clouds are a sign of rain, so the prediction is yes with the reason.

questions.questionText: The pupils carry their umbrellas. Will it rain?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because they get ready for rain.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the sea is blue.

questions.explanation: Choose the word or reply that fits the meaning and the grammar.

questions.questionText: Grandma looks at the black clouds. She says it will rain. Why?
questions.explanation: Choose the word or reply that fits the meaning and the grammar.

questions.questionText: The wind blows hard and the leaves fly. What will happen?
questions.explanation: Choose the word or reply that fits the meaning and the grammar.

questions.questionText: The sky is blue and the sun is bright. Will it rain now?

options.label: A

questions.explanation: We say good at doing something.

questions.questionText: The picture hangs ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: We say a picture hangs on the wall.

questions.questionText: This is ___ umbrella. It is new.
questions.explanation: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so we use an.

questions.questionText: ___ are my shoes over there by the door.
questions.explanation: Over there means far, so we use Those.

questions.questionText: Read the poem: "Rain on the window, rain on the tree, rain on the flowers, not on me!" What does the rain fall on?
questions.explanation: The poem says the rain falls on the window, the tree and the flowers.

questions.questionText: Read: "The little cat jumps high, it jumps up to the sky, it lands on the mat, and purrs like that." Where does the cat land?
questions.explanation: The poem says the cat lands on the mat.

questions.questionText: Read: "I like bread and butter, I like milk and honey, I like rice and curry, yummy in my tummy." What does the writer like?
questions.explanation: The poem says: I like bread and butter.

questions.questionText: Read: "Buzzy bee, buzzy bee, on the clover, come to me, drink the nectar, sweet and slow, where the pretty clovers grow." Where does the bee rest?
questions.explanation: The poem says the bee is on the clover.

questions.questionText: Read: "The moon is a silver boat, it sails in the sky at night, the stars are little lamps, they shine so soft and bright." What is the moon compared to?
questions.explanation: The poem says: The moon is a silver boat.

questions.questionText: Read: "The tree stands tall and green, it keeps the ground so clean, birds build nests up in its arms, and hide away from storms." Who builds nests in the tree?
questions.explanation: The poem says birds build nests in the tree.

questions.questionText: In the line "rain on the flowers, not on me!", what does not on me mean?

options.label: A
options.text: the writer does not want rain on himself

options.label: C
options.text: the writer plays in the rain

options.label: D
options.text: the writer sings in the rain

questions.explanation: Not on me means the writer does not want the rain on him.

questions.questionText: In "it lands on the mat, and purrs like that", the word purrs is a sound made by a ___.
questions.explanation: Cats make a soft purring sound.

questions.questionText: Read again: "The little cat jumps high, it jumps up to the sky, it lands on the mat, and purrs like that." Which word rhymes with high?
questions.explanation: High and sky rhyme.

questions.questionText: Read: "I like bread and butter, I like milk and honey, I like rice and curry, yummy in my tummy." Which word rhymes with honey?
questions.explanation: Honey and tummy rhyme.

questions.questionText: Read: "Buzzy bee, buzzy bee, on the clover, come to me, drink the nectar, sweet and slow, where the pretty clovers grow." Which word rhymes with bee?
questions.explanation: Bee and me rhyme.

questions.questionText: Read: "The moon is a silver boat, it sails in the sky at night, the stars are little lamps, they shine so soft and bright." Which word rhymes with night?
questions.explanation: Night and bright rhyme.

questions.questionText: In "it sails in the sky at night", the idea of sails tells us the moon ___ across the sky.
questions.explanation: A boat sails slowly on water; here the moon sails slowly across the sky.

questions.questionText: In "yummy in my tummy", the word yummy means the food is ___.
questions.explanation: Yummy means tasty and nice to eat.

questions.questionText: In "drink the nectar, sweet and slow", nectar is ___.
questions.explanation: Bees drink nectar, the sweet juice inside flowers.

questions.questionText: In "and hide away from storms", storms are ___ weather.
questions.explanation: Storms bring bad, windy, rainy weather.

questions.questionText: "Rain on the window, rain on the tree, rain on the flowers" describes rain that is ___.
questions.explanation: The rain falls on many things around, so it is falling gently everywhere.

questions.questionText: In "it jumps up to the sky", the cat jumps so high it seems to reach the sky. This shows the cat is ___.
questions.explanation: Jumping high and purring shows the cat is playful and lively.

questions.questionText: The poet calls the stars little lamps. This comparison tells us the stars are ___.
questions.explanation: Lamps give light, so the stars are small bright lights in the sky.

questions.questionText: "The tree stands tall and green, it keeps the ground so clean." This line tells us the tree ___ the place.
questions.explanation: Trees give shade and help keep the ground green, clean and cool.

questions.questionText: A song says: "Clap your hands, stomp your feet, turn around and take a seat." What do you do first?
questions.explanation: The song starts with Clap your hands.

questions.questionText: The song goes: "Jump up high, reach the sky, bend down low and touch your knee." Which action makes you tall?
questions.explanation: Jumping up high makes you stretch tall.

questions.questionText: "Wave your left hand, wave your right, left foot out and left foot in." Which body part do you wave first?
questions.explanation: The song says wave your left hand first.

questions.questionText: "Nod your head, blink your eyes, smile so wide and look surprised." What does nod your head mean?

options.label: B
options.text: move your head up and down

questions.explanation: Nodding means moving your head up and down.

questions.questionText: Your friend sings: "Touch your nose!" What do you do?
questions.explanation: You do the action the song names.

questions.questionText: The teacher says: "Now, everyone, hop on one foot!" What do you do?
questions.explanation: You follow the action the teacher asks for.

questions.questionText: "Put your right hand in, take your right hand out, shake it all about." This song is about ___.
questions.explanation: The actions are dance movements.

questions.questionText: "Hop like a rabbit, jump like a frog, crawl like a snail, slow like a log." Which animal moves very slowly?
questions.explanation: A snail moves very slowly.

questions.questionText: "Stretch up tall like a rubber band, curl up small like a ball on sand." When you curl up small, you ___.

options.label: C
options.text: make your body tiny and round

questions.explanation: Curling up makes your body small and round like a ball.

questions.questionText: "March, march, on the spot, stop right now when you hear the clap." What should you do when you hear a clap?
questions.explanation: The song says stop when you hear the clap.

questions.questionText: Your friend does a funny dance and invites you to join. What do you say?
questions.explanation: A nice way to join in is to say it looks fun.

questions.questionText: You are playing a song game and you make a mistake. What do you say?
questions.explanation: We laugh, say sorry and try again.

questions.questionText: In a dance game, the music suddenly stops. What do you do?
questions.explanation: In a freeze dance, you stop when the music stops.

questions.questionText: "Fly like a bird up in the blue, swim like a fish in the cool sea too." This song asks you to imagine ___.
questions.explanation: You imagine being a bird, then a fish.

questions.questionText: "When the sun comes up, we stretch and play, when the sun goes down, we end the day." This song is about ___.

options.label: A
options.text: a day from morning to night

questions.explanation: It moves from sunrise in the morning to sunset at night.

questions.questionText: You give half your orange to a friend. You are ___.
questions.explanation: Giving part of what you have to a friend is sharing.

questions.questionText: A ___ person always tells the truth.
questions.explanation: An honest person tells the truth.

questions.questionText: We speak ___ to our teachers and elders.
questions.explanation: We speak politely to teachers and elders.

questions.questionText: A ___ student studies hard and finishes homework on time.
questions.explanation: A hardworking student works hard and finishes work on time.

questions.questionText: We ___ our elders by listening when they speak.
questions.explanation: We show respect by listening to our elders.

questions.questionText: A ___ friend says kind words when someone is sad.
questions.explanation: A kind person helps others feel better.

questions.questionText: "Please share your snacks with your sister." Here share means ___.

options.label: D
options.text: give a part of to her

questions.explanation: Sharing means letting others have part of what you have.

questions.questionText: "Be polite when you speak to the guest." Polite means we have ___ manners.
questions.explanation: Polite means having good manners.

questions.questionText: You take a classmate pencil by mistake. You say sorry and return it. This shows you are ___.
questions.explanation: Saying sorry and making it right is being honest.

questions.questionText: Please and thank you are words we use to be ___.
questions.explanation: Using please and thank you shows good manners.

questions.questionText: Classmates work together to clean the classroom. They show ___.
questions.explanation: Working together shows care and teamwork.

questions.questionText: A boy helps an old lady carry her bag across the road. He is being ___.
questions.explanation: Helping someone is kind and helpful.

questions.questionText: You break a cup and tell your mother at once. You are ___.
questions.explanation: Telling the truth even when you are wrong is honest.

questions.questionText: The ___ girl practises the piano every evening.
questions.explanation: Practising every day shows hard work.

questions.questionText: "We respect our grandparents." Here respect means we ___ them.
questions.explanation: Respecting grandparents means treating them with care.

questions.questionText: "The honest boy gave back the extra change." Honest shows he did not ___ the money.
questions.explanation: An honest person does not keep what is not his.

questions.questionText: "The hardworking student scored well in the test." Hardworking means she ___.
questions.explanation: Hard work means trying your best.

questions.questionText: Your friend wins a race and you clap for her. You show ___.
questions.explanation: Praising a friend win shows respect and good sportsmanship.

questions.questionText: You see a new pupil sitting alone at recess. You invite him to play with you. This shows ___.
questions.explanation: Inviting someone who is alone is kind.

questions.questionText: A hardworking farmer wakes up early every day to tend his plants. This tells us he ___.

options.label: A
options.text: does his work carefully and on time

questions.explanation: Waking up early and working shows hard work and care.

questions.questionText: Which word begins with a capital letter because it is a person name?
questions.explanation: Mei is a person name, so it starts with a capital letter.

questions.questionText: Which word is the special name of a day?
questions.explanation: Monday is the special name of a day.

questions.questionText: Which word is a general word rather than a special name?
questions.explanation: School is a general word; the others are special names.

questions.questionText: Which word is the special name of a month?
questions.explanation: January is the special name of a month.

questions.questionText: Which word is a general name for an animal?
questions.explanation: Elephant is a general word for an animal.

questions.questionText: Which word must begin with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: Days of the week, like Tuesday, begin with capital letters.

questions.questionText: Which word is a person name?
questions.explanation: Devi is a person name.

questions.questionText: Which word begins with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: April is a month name, so it begins with a capital letter.

questions.questionText: Which word is a place in the sentence "Devi visits Langkawi in December"?
questions.explanation: Langkawi is the name of a place.

questions.questionText: Which word is NOT a special name?
questions.explanation: Pencil is a general word; the others are special names.

questions.questionText: A boy says: "I live in Johor." Which word is a place?
questions.explanation: Johor is the name of a place.

questions.questionText: Which word is a shop name in "We eat noodles at Restoran Sin Lean"?
questions.explanation: Restoran Sin Lean is the special name of a shop.

questions.questionText: Which word is the special name of a festival?
questions.explanation: Hari Merdeka is the special name of a festival.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has BOTH a person name and a day name?

options.label: A
options.text: The market is big and busy.

options.label: C
options.text: Mei goes to the market on Saturday.

questions.explanation: Mei is a person name and Saturday is a day name.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the capital letters correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: My cousin plays badminton on wednesday.

options.label: B
options.text: my cousin Rani plays badminton on Wednesday.

options.label: C
options.text: My cousin rani plays badminton on Wednesday.

options.label: D
options.text: My cousin Rani plays badminton on Wednesday.

questions.explanation: Both the name Rani and the day Wednesday need capital letters.
